_comment: Cost is computed from tokens, not from a rounded per-image price: tokens_per_image x usd_per_million_output_tokens / 1e6. Google publishes both, and the rounded figures drift (4K computes to $0.1512 but is published as $0.151, and Vertex rounds it to $0.15). Over thousands of images that drift compounds, so the token count is the source of truth.
_verified_note: Every number below is quoted verbatim from Google's pricing page footnotes. Nothing here is inferred. Gaps are left null rather than extrapolated.

gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image.label: Nano Banana 2 Lite
gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image._gap: Google publishes a token count for 1K only. 512/2K/4K are deliberately null: gemini-3-pro-image proves the token curve differs per model, so extrapolating from Flash Image would be a guess.

gemini-3-pro-image.label: Nano Banana Pro
gemini-3-pro-image._note: 1K and 2K cost the same here (both 1120 tokens), and 4K is 2000 tokens rather than 2520. This model has its own curve.

gemini-2.5-flash-image.label: Nano Banana (legacy)
gemini-2.5-flash-image._gap: Priced per image up to 1024x1024 only. Google publishes no token count above that, so higher resolutions are null.
